title: Simple Table

illustrates.rule: 11.2.1-11.2.2 (no explicit "See Example" cross-reference; positioned immediately after Example 11-1 and before rule 11.2.3, illustrating ordinary table transcription and the General Format rules of 11.2.5 that follow later on the same/next page)
illustrates.quote: Tables are transcribed as they are in print if possible and alternate methods are used when that is not possible.

print.surroundingText: 11.2.4 ("Related columns show a relationship between entries across a row of columns but no relationship between entries in one row with entries in another row.") follows the example.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box with a ruled line under the header row. Header row ("Animal", "Longest Life Span") is bold. Data rows alternate light-blue shading (mosquito, elephant rows shaded; gorilla row unshaded) — decorative, not meaningful.

braille.notes: Blank braille-cell line before the top box line and after the bottom box line, matching Formats §11.2.5.d's blank-line-before/after-table rule even though this table is boxed. Column heading 'Longest Life Span' is abbreviated to 'life span' in braille with no transcriber's note (lowercased, per 11.7.1.c which permits uppercase-to-lowercase conversion without a note); guide dots (dot 5, rendered as ") pad each entry out to the separation-line width.

resolution: No content differences; header schema normalized to a list-of-lists. pdfPages/width agreed and were confirmed against the page-boundary map and box-rule length.

corrections.source: page image (PDF text layer drops one of two spaces)
corrections.note: K33: the gold was transcribed from a text dump of the PDF that collapses a run of exactly two blank cells to one (and in some lines adds spurious blanks). Line(s) 3, 4, 6 rewritten to the book's exact cell positions, measured from the SimBraille glyph origins on PDF page 285 and checked cell by cell against the 300 dpi page image (blank vs dotted cell). What changed: two blank cells collapsed to one (3). Where: column gap (table / related columns / columned list) (2); table separation line (1).
